```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(OncoCohortSelect)
```

Two single-arm cohorts, Cohort1 and Cohort2, are run in parallel, and one of
them is to be selected for further development. Cohort2 is the default, and
Cohort1 is selected only if the data favor it. This vignette compares decision
rules based on the posterior benefit-risk score and on win statistics by their
selection probabilities in simulated trials.

## What makes a rule better

The scores of the two approaches are on different scales, so their raw values
cannot be compared. A fair comparison fixes, for every rule, the probability
of selecting Cohort1 when it is not better than Cohort2 (here, identical
cohorts), and then compares the probabilities of selecting Cohort1 when it is
better. The truth must be defined before the simulation and independently of
the rules: by scenarios in which the better cohort is clear (one cohort at
least as good on every endpoint), and, for trade-offs between efficacy and
safety, by the choice the clinical team would make for the true parameters.

## Scenarios

Each scenario gives the true parameters of the two cohorts: PFS and OS
medians, response rate and adverse event rate. The number of simulated trials
is kept small so that the vignette builds quickly; an evaluation would use
several thousand.

```{r}
make_arm <- function(pfs, orr, os) {
  CorOncoEndpoints::OncoArm(pfs.median = pfs, orr = orr, resp.cor = 0.4,
                            death.prop = 0.15, os.median = os)
}
scenarios <- list(
  "Identical" = list(arms = list(Cohort1 = make_arm(6, 0.30, 15),
                                 Cohort2 = make_arm(6, 0.30, 15)), ae = c(0.20, 0.20)),
  "Cohort1 better" = list(arms = list(Cohort1 = make_arm(9, 0.50, 20),
                                      Cohort2 = make_arm(6, 0.30, 15)), ae = c(0.20, 0.20)),
  "Cohort1 better, more AE" = list(arms = list(Cohort1 = make_arm(9, 0.50, 20),
                                               Cohort2 = make_arm(6, 0.30, 15)),
                                   ae = c(0.40, 0.20)))
nsim <- 200
```

## Rules

The benefit-risk score against target values is computed for each cohort, and
Cohort1 is selected when its score exceeds that of Cohort2 by more than a
threshold (`br_diff`). The score of Cohort1 relative to Cohort2 selects Cohort1
when it exceeds a threshold (`br_ref`). The net treatment benefit (`ntb`) and
the win ratio (`wr`) of the pairwise comparisons with priority OS, PFS,
response and adverse event select Cohort1 when they exceed a threshold.

```{r}
eps <- list(
  Endpoint("OS", "tte", time = "os_tte", event = "os_event"),
  Endpoint("PFS", "tte", time = "pfs_tte", event = "pfs_event"),
  Endpoint("ORR", "binary", var = "response"),
  Endpoint("AE", "binary", var = "ae", higher.better = FALSE))
crit <- data.frame(endpoint = c("ORR", "PFS", "OS", "AE"),
                   target = c(0.30, 0.50, 0.60, 0.30), time = c(NA, 6, 12, NA))
crit_ref <- data.frame(endpoint = c("ORR", "PFS", "OS", "AE"),
                       measure = c("rate", "hr", "hr", "rate"),
                       target = c(0.10, 0.80, 0.90, 0.10))
```

Each scenario is simulated with 50 patients per cohort, enrolled over 12
months and analyzed at month 24.

```{r}
res <- lapply(seq_along(scenarios), function(i) {
  sc <- scenarios[[i]]
  d <- SimCohorts(nsim = nsim, n = c(50, 50), arms = sc$arms, ae.rate = sc$ae,
                  cutoff = 24, a.time = c(0, 12), seed = i)
  SimSelection(d, eps, crit, treatment = "Cohort1", control = "Cohort2",
               criteria.ref = crit_ref)
})
names(res) <- names(scenarios)
head(res[["Cohort1 better"]][, c("br_trt", "br_ctl", "br_ref", "ntb", "wr")])
```

## Thresholds and selection probabilities

The thresholds are calibrated in the scenario with identical cohorts so that
Cohort1 is selected in at most 10% of the trials.

```{r}
stats <- c("br_diff", "br_ref", "ntb", "wr")
thr <- do.call(rbind, lapply(stats, function(s) {
  CalibrateThreshold(res[["Identical"]], s, alpha = 0.10)
}))
thr
tab <- sapply(names(res), function(sc) {
  vapply(seq_along(stats), function(i) {
    SelectionOC(res[[sc]], stats[i], threshold = thr$threshold[i])$p_treatment
  }, numeric(1))
})
rownames(tab) <- stats
knitr::kable(tab, digits = 2,
             caption = "Probability of selecting Cohort1 at the calibrated thresholds")
```

In the scenario "Cohort1 better", the rules select Cohort1 with probabilities
between `r round(min(tab[, "Cohort1 better"]), 2)` and
`r round(max(tab[, "Cohort1 better"]), 2)`. With more adverse events in
Cohort1, the probabilities range from
`r round(min(tab[, "Cohort1 better, more AE"]), 2)` to
`r round(max(tab[, "Cohort1 better, more AE"]), 2)`; whether Cohort1 should be
selected in that scenario is a clinical judgment that has to be fixed before
the rules are compared.

## Saturation of the score against target values

In the scenario "Cohort1 better", the median scores against the target values
are `r round(median(res[["Cohort1 better"]]$br_trt), 3)` for Cohort1 and
`r round(median(res[["Cohort1 better"]]$br_ctl), 3)` for Cohort2. The score
measures how certainly a cohort exceeds the targets, not by how much. When both
cohorts clearly exceed the targets, both scores approach 1 and their difference
carries little information; the score relative to the other cohort and the win
statistics compare the cohorts directly.

```{r}
summary(res[["Cohort1 better"]][, c("br_trt", "br_ctl")])
```
